summary: Verified Gemini retry/fallback resilience in backend/routers/temp_transactions.py via unit tests with monkeypatched _gemini() (no real API key needed) plus a live endpoint smoke test. All 5 tests pass.
critical_code_review_comments: Backoff sleep uses blocking time.sleep inside a sync function called via asyncio.to_thread — acceptable since it runs off the event loop; fine as-is.

_FALLBACK_MODELS length is 4 and each attempts 3 retries → worst-case up to 12 API calls with 1.5s+3s sleeps per model (~13.5s of blocking sleep). Consider reducing retries per fallback model, or only retrying on the PRIMARY and single-attempting fallbacks, to keep worst-case latency lower.
_is_transient() substring-matches '500' which will also match strings like '5000' or '500ms' — very small risk of false-positive classification. Consider regex word-boundary matching.
Non-transient errors raise immediately (good), but if the FIRST model returns non-transient (e.g. schema issue), fallback models are never tried — this is intended per spec and confirmed by Case C.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tests cover: (A) transient-then-success recovers within 3 retries on primary model, (B) persistent 503 exhausts all fallback models and raises friendly RuntimeError containing 'sibuk'/'503', (C) non-transient ValueError propagates after exactly 1 call (no retry, no fallback), plus (D) /api/temp-transactions/upload returns HTTP 400 with detail containing 'GEMINI_API_KEY' when key is empty and (E) backend still healthy afterwards. Login uses cookie-based session (POST /api/auth/login sets HTTPOnly cookie; no bearer token in response body). Tests monkeypatch temp_transactions.time.sleep to no-op for speed.
